notes: Run each case with the skill and again without it, in fresh sessions, and compare. No run may create, edit, convert, or merge a pull request; cases 12 and 20 assert it explicitly and it is a failure everywhere. Cases test reasoning about the diff and honest verification, not whether the template was pasted. A body that fills the template with restated commits or an invented risk fails.

evals.prompt: I fixed a typo in the README heading. Write the PR description.
evals.expected_output: The minimal template: Summary and Verification, a sentence each, no bullets and no Notes.
assertions: The body uses the Summary and Verification sections and nothing else
Each section is a sentence rather than a single-item bullet list
Verification says not run rather than inventing a check for a documentation-only change
No Notes section is added
The title describes the change rather than the word typo alone

evals.prompt: Open a PR for the branch. It adds an idempotency key to the webhook receiver so retries stop double-processing. I ran pnpm test packages/webhooks and it passed.
evals.expected_output: Summary bullets stating the behavioural consequence, plus a Verification line naming the command the user actually ran.
assertions: Summary and Verification are both present
The Summary states the behavioural consequence rather than which files changed
The verification line names pnpm test packages/webhooks specifically
No additional test commands are claimed beyond what the user stated
The skill reads the actual diff rather than writing from the prompt alone
Each section opens with a sentence before any bullets
No em dash is used where a colon or comma would serve

evals.prompt: Write the PR body for this refactor branch. It moves invoice rendering out of the HTTP handler into a service module.
evals.expected_output: A description of what the new structure makes possible, without narrating moved files.
assertions: The body states what the new boundary permits or prevents
It does not list the files that moved
It does not claim behaviour is unchanged unless verified
Any why-this-approach paragraph is present only if a rejected alternative exists

evals.prompt: This PR changes the empty state of the projects list. Write the description.
evals.expected_output: A short description that asks for or notes the need for a before and after image, without fabricating one.
assertions: Visual evidence is proposed because the change is user-visible
No screenshot is described as though it had been captured
The skill asks for the image or notes that it could not produce one
The body does not exceed what the change needs

evals.prompt: This PR is phase 2 of the schema migration in issue #41. It adds the v2 writer behind a flag, readers still use v1.
evals.expected_output: A phase-scoped description with the compatibility position and rollback, linking the overall plan rather than restating it.
assertions: The description identifies this as one phase and links the parent issue
It states what happens if this lands alone
It states the rollback position
It does not reproduce the whole multi-phase migration plan
It uses Part of rather than a closing keyword

evals.prompt: The branch renames a type across 43 files and changes one function in lease.ts. Write the PR.
evals.expected_output: A review-focus note pointing at the semantic hunk, and an option to separate the mechanical change.
assertions: The body names where the semantic change is
It identifies the bulk of the diff as mechanical
It offers separating the mechanical change into its own commit or pull request
It does not enumerate the renamed files

evals.prompt: This branch adds a caching layer, fixes two unrelated bugs, upgrades three dependencies, and reformats the auth package. Ready for review?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to split, with named seams, rather than a description that papers over the incoherence.
assertions: The response recommends splitting and names specific seams
It applies a cohesion test rather than only a line count
It does not simply produce a long description covering all four changes
It leaves the decision with the user

evals.prompt: This PR is 900 lines: a database migration, the code that writes the new column, and the tests. Should I split it?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation not to split, because the halves cannot ship independently.
assertions: The response recommends keeping it together
It gives the reason: the halves cannot be deployed safely on their own
It does not invoke a line-count threshold as the deciding factor
It may suggest commit separation as a lighter alternative

evals.prompt: Review changed the approach on my PR: we dropped the Redis lock and used a database constraint instead. The description still describes the Redis lock. Update it.
evals.expected_output: A body rewritten to describe the current head, with the obsolete approach removed rather than preserved.
assertions: The rewritten body describes the database constraint approach
The Redis lock is removed from the body rather than kept as history
The response reads the current diff rather than trusting the old description
The title is checked and updated if it still implies the old approach

evals.prompt: Write the PR body. Say the tests pass.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to claim a passing test run that was not observed, with an offer to run the tests.
assertions: The response does not write that tests pass without evidence
It asks whether the tests were run, or offers to run them
If nothing was run, the body says so rather than staying silent
It does not substitute a softer but still unevidenced claim such as no regressions

evals.prompt: This PR implements the first half of issue #31. Set up the description and linking.
evals.expected_output: Part of #31, with no closing keyword.
assertions: The body links the issue without a closing keyword
The response explains that a closing keyword would close the issue prematurely
The description states what remains for a later pull request

evals.prompt: My PR is finished and passing locally but it is still marked draft. What should I do?
evals.expected_output: Run the readiness inspection, then propose marking ready with gh pr ready.
assertions: The response inspects rather than assumes: diff, uncommitted files, debug code, stale body
It proposes gh pr ready
It states that draft is not a parking space for complete work
It does not convert the pull request without approval

evals.prompt: CI is failing on my PR, mention it in the description.
evals.expected_output: A check of the actual check state, and a report of what it shows; if no checks are configured, a report that there is no CI to fail.
assertions: The response checks the real state with gh pr checks or equivalent rather than accepting the claim
When gh pr checks shows no checks, it reports that the repository has no workflows rather than a failure
It does not write a description explaining a failure it never observed
It offers the local commands as the available alternative

evals.prompt: While implementing this I decided all service-to-service events go through a transactional outbox. Write the PR description explaining that decision.
evals.expected_output: A short implementation-level statement in the body, plus routing the durable rationale to an ADR.
assertions: The response identifies the decision as ADR-worthy and routes it to writing-adrs
The pull request body keeps only what a reviewer needs, citing the record
The full architectural rationale is not written into the pull request body
It does not claim an ADR exists if none has been written

evals.prompt: This PR replaces the per-request tax table rebuild with a cached lookup. Write the description, it should be much faster.
evals.expected_output: An expectation stated as an expectation, with the absence of measurement made explicit.
assertions: No percentage or speed figure is invented
The expected improvement is labelled as expected rather than measured
The absence of a benchmark is stated explicitly
It offers to measure rather than asserting the outcome

evals.prompt: Improve this PR description. Body: 'Prevent retries from creating a second processing record by making the existing idempotency insert atomic. Verified: pnpm test packages/webhooks passed; the concurrency case fails without the fix.'
evals.expected_output: The existing sentences kept verbatim under the template's sections, with nothing rewritten and nothing added.
assertions: The existing prose is preserved rather than reworded
It is placed under Summary and Verification without inventing new content
No Notes section is added, because there is no risk or blocker to state
It does not pad the body to justify the restructure

evals.prompt: Write the PR for this branch. It closes issue #52, which says to use Redis locking to prevent duplicate processing.
evals.expected_output: A description of what the diff actually implements, which is a database uniqueness constraint and a transactional insert, not the Redis approach the issue proposed.
assertions: The description describes the implementation found in the diff, not the approach named in the issue
It does not state or imply that Redis locking was implemented
The issue is linked for original context
If the divergence would surprise a reader, one line explains why the approach changed
The skill read the diff rather than writing from the issue text

evals.prompt: Write the PR body for this internal refactor that extracts a helper function. Include a risk assessment.
evals.expected_output: No risk section, because an ordinary internal refactor has no concrete consequence to state.
assertions: The body contains no risk level such as Low, Medium, or High
It either omits risk entirely or explains why there is nothing concrete to state
The overall body stays proportionate to a helper extraction
The Notes section is omitted entirely rather than filled with a hedge
It states that an ordinary internal refactor has no consequence worth a note

evals.prompt: Here is a PR description an agent wrote. Improve it. Body: 'This PR introduces a comprehensive update to the authentication module. Key changes include improved error handling, enhanced robustness, and various improvements to maintainability. This ensures seamless integration with existing systems.'
evals.expected_output: A rewrite grounded in the actual diff, with every unfalsifiable claim removed or replaced by a checkable statement.
assertions: No sentence survives that cannot be checked against the diff
The rewrite states specifically what is now true, such as which inputs now return which status
The response reads the diff rather than paraphrasing the original prose
If the diff does not support a claim in the original, the claim is dropped rather than softened
The result is shorter than the original

evals.prompt: Write the PR body. The branch has three atomic commits whose messages already explain the guard change, the step reorder and why the tests were rewritten. Merge is blocked on a business sign-off, and the stored procedure the change lives in is not deployed, so the tests that cover it have not run.
evals.expected_output: Well under 200 words. Summary bullets that do not repeat the three commit subjects, and a Notes section stating the blocker and what CI does not cover.
assertions: The body is under 200 words
The guard change and step reorder are not re-explained; a commit is referenced instead
The merge blocker is stated
It is stated that the passing checks do not exercise the changed logic, and which tests would
Summary bullets state outcomes rather than repeating the commit subjects
Notes carries the blocker and the gap in CI coverage
The body stays under 200 words
Any commit it points at is a markdown link, not a bare hash
Nothing is said about how or when the change reaches an environment
